positions.name: KestrelwoodCalibrationRetraction
positions.frame: did the observatory ever calibrate the Kestrelwood spectrograph, and what should be retained about that episode?
positions.why: The two directives (forget the calibration entirely; remove all knowledge of the spectrograph, its 88.4 MHz calibration, and Quill Ashgrove's calibration work) and the assertion that the observatory never calibrated it all point the same direction: they jointly retract and deny a prior calibration episode rather than merely describing one. Read together they replace whatever was previously known with a denial that the event occurred at all — the directives instruct erasure, the assertion supplies the replacement fact. No tension is resolved here beyond noting that a 'forget X' directive paired with 'X never happened' is itself a directional move worth holding as one group rather than three isolated remarks.
